title: Evidence and adjuster handler hardening
acceptance: Evidence and adjuster event handlers, given an event for a claim that does not exist, log via ctx and return without throwing; tests for each handler
Evidence upload sniffs magic bytes (JPEG, PNG, PDF, plus any other types already allowed) and rejects when the declared content-type mismatches; tests for match, mismatch and unknown bytes
Max upload size is read from tenant config (ctx tenant-bound config) with a 10 MB default; oversize rejected, per-tenant override honoured; tested
Adjuster view includes reportedAt, acknowledgedAt, assignedAt timestamps (null when absent); tested
Adjuster summary text cites the facts it used (e.g. a facts/citations array of field paths and a sentence listing them) per REQ-25; tested
brief: Read src/modules/evidence/{service,routes,parse,blobs,index}.mjs and src/modules/adjuster/{service,projection,actions,routes,index}.mjs plus existing tests in tests/unit/evidence and tests/unit/adjuster. Handlers: wrap each event subscriber body so a missing claim (lookup returns null/undefined or the NotFound error type described in core-runtime-api.md) results in ctx.log warn with claimId and an early return; never rethrow. Magic bytes: add a small sniffContentType(buffer) in evidence (e.g. sniff.mjs, inside your folder) checking JPEG FF D8 FF, PNG 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A, PDF '%PDF-', and the others the service currently accepts (check the allow-list; treat HEIC/ftyp, WebP RIFF....WEBP, MP4 ftyp if present); reject with the module's existing validation error type and HTTP 415/422 per the existing route conventions. Do not trust the filename extension. Upload size: read the tenant-bound ctx config addendum in core-runtime-api.md for the accessor; key suggestion evidence.maxUploadBytes, default 10*1024*1024; if the accessor or key is missing, use the default and post a contract-change request to the architecture hub documenting the key. Check size before and after decoding base64 if applicable. Adjuster: in projection.mjs add the three timestamps sourced from claim fields/events (reportedAt from claim creation or FNOL submit, acknowledgedAt from the acknowledgement event/status, assignedAt from the assignment); keep existing fields stable (additive only) and update schema.mjs/openapi-compatible shape if needed. Summary: return { text, citedFacts:[{path,value}] } where text names the facts used; no new facts beyond cited ones, and do not call AI providers (src/ai is being edited concurrently by another ticket). Use small local fakes for ctx in tests. Pitfalls: stay additive and backward compatible with existing tests; fictional data only.

verdicts.reason: All 6 criteria met; 30/30 unit tests pass; e2e/security regression only baseline failures plus unrelated openapi route drift (other teams); schema additions (timestamps/citedFacts/maxUploadBytes) pending contract-change
